title: introduce-stall-resume-workload-fuzzer-and-compact-telemetry-serializer
author: Aisha Malik
description:
Motivation: production inference tails show short, stochastic stalls followed by recovery bursts that amplify p95/p99. Existing synthetic runners model bursts and steady-state churn but do not reliably recreate short stall-and-resume patterns observed in dedicated clusters. This PR adds a small, composable workload fuzzer (stall-resume-fuzzer) and a compact telemetry serializer to capture high-fidelity traces with low bandwidth impact for long runs.

Summary of changes: implemented a configurable StallResume workload component that injects randomized micro-stalls into multi-sequence batched traffic, a ReplayHarness that can replay recorded stall sequences deterministically with optional time-scaling, and a compact protobuf-based TelemetrySerializer that encodes per-token latency deltas, KV-cache checkpoint markers and device steering hints (node id, queue depth). Also added an end-to-end benchmark scenario and short docs + quickstart.

Checklist: [x] implement fuzzer core, [x] add deterministic replay mode, [x] add serializer + backward-compatible schema v1, [x] integrate with CI perf job (nightly), [x] add docs and example config, [x] smoke test on r3-dedicated cluster.

Why this is different: unlike the existing burst and primer runners, this harness targets sub-10ms stalls that are intermittent and correlated with device scheduling and kernel preemption. The ReplayHarness supports resume policies (soft-resume, hard-resume) and an option to steer the replay to specific device types to reproduce heterogeneous-device edge cases. The compact serializer is optimized for long-duration runs by delta-encoding latencies and pruning redundant KV-checkpoint frames, reducing telemetry size by ~6x in our internal pilot.

Design notes: the fuzzer composes as a traffic wrapper (implements Runner interface) and exposes: - stall_rate (events/sec), - stall_duration_dist (exp|pareto|fixed), - affected_fraction (percent of concurrent sequences), - seed for RNG for deterministic runs. ReplayHarness accepts serialized traces and can replay with time_scale and device_map. TelemetrySerializer v1 uses a small proto schema with varint delta-encoding and optional zstd chunking. Backwards compatibility: serializer emits a top-level 'schema_version' header.

Testing & CI: unit tests for determinism and serializer roundtrip included. Nightly perf job added to .github/workflows/benchmark-nightly.yaml that runs the stall-resume scenario for 45m on a 3-node mini-cluster; the job was flaky initially due to nondeterministic RNG seeding in the harness, fixed by seeding per-run using the provided seed param and adding a deterministic shuffle step. Final CI: 12 checks (build, linters, unit tests, flake8, mypy-like static checks, container image build, nightly-scheduling smoke) all passed on rerun.

Commits summary: see commits below for details.

Files changed (high level): src/runners/stall_resume_runner.py, src/harness/replay_harness.py, src/telemetry/compact_serializer.py, protos/telemetry/v1/compact.proto, examples/stall_resume/configs/minimal.yaml, docs/bench/stall_resume.md, .github/workflows/benchmark-nightly.yaml, tests/test_stall_resume.py, tests/test_serializer_roundtrip.py, perf/fixtures/stall_traces/sample_trace.v1.cpt, scripts/convert_trace_to_json.sh

Release notes: Adds new experimental StallResume workload fuzzer and ReplayHarness with deterministic replay. Adds a compact telemetry serializer (v1) for long-duration benchmarks. This is experimental (opt-in) and behind a feature flag in bench configs.

Related: ENG-1829 (investigate short stall p99 regressions), ENG-2150 (nightly perf scenarios expansion).

Merge: squash-merged to main after approval.
